issues.translation_quote: Tick-tock!
issues.justification: "Тики-так" is thieves' slang for "okay/all right" (explicitly glossed later as 'Хорошо? - Тики-так'). Rendering it as "Tick-tock" is meaningless in English and ruins the slang-lesson gag.

issues.translation_quote: A not-so-good person? - A radish.
issues.justification: "Not-so-good person" is a stilted literal rendering of the euphemistic 'нехороший человек'; repeated throughout (Cross-Eye, 'not-so-good person'), it sounds unnatural. The joke of the Docent's euphemism vs. slang is weakened; 'bad egg'/'rotten apple' would work better.

issues.translation_quote: Ego: A robbery? - A stick-up.
issues.justification: Acceptable here, but the nearby 'Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея' is left as untranslated 'Frey-feya' with no explanation; the gag (Fedya forgetting a slang word, 'фрей' ≈ good guy) is lost on English viewers.

issues.translation_quote: You, kind of... Kind of what?
issues.justification: Acceptable overall, but the Docent's comic confrontation is flattened; minor rendering inaccuracies reduce the effect.

issues.source_quote: Какие еще змеи? - Кобры. - Уложи верблюда! - Ляг! Ложись, дядя!
issues.translation_quote: Make the camel lie down! - Down! Lie down, mister!
issues.justification: 'Дядя' addressed to the camel is a humorous familiar address; 'mister' is odd. Also 'Доцент' as a nickname rendered as 'Docent' is unfamiliar in English; the nickname's irony (a thug called 'Docent', a title for a lecturer) is not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Автомашину куплю с магнитофоном, пошью костюм с отливом и в Ялту!
issues.translation_quote: This ain’t lifting wallets… I'll buy a car with a tape recorder, get a shiny suit made, and off to Yalta!
issues.justification: 'Это тебе не мелочь по карманам тырить' is rendered with an added ellipsis and 'ain't' register not matching the rest; the sentence is also truncated in sense (a big heist vs. petty pickpocketing).

issues.source_quote: Я злой и страшный серый волк, я в поросятах знаю толк.
issues.translation_quote: I’m the Big Bad Wolf, and I know a piglet or two!
issues.justification: The rhyming children's song parody ('Nobody fears the grey wolf') is only partly preserved; the original rhyme and the cultural reference to the Russian version are lost.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: The others are doing time in Central Asia, and he's near Moscow.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Не с чем' translated as 'Don't.' loses the meaning 'nothing to congratulate on'.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший ты человек, Косой, злой, как собака.
issues.translation_quote: You're a not-so-good person, Cross-Eye, mean as a dog.
issues.justification: Literal rendering of a euphemism used as a running gag; sounds unnatural in English.

issues.translation_quote: You'd better find the helmet.
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Вася' broken English lines are inconsistent with the Russian, where Vasya speaks broken Russian only at times.

issues.translation_quote: - Yes, yes. IRS.
issues.justification: ОБХС is the Soviet anti-embezzlement police unit; 'IRS' is an incorrect cultural substitution, and the joke (the crook mistaking English 'yes' for the police acronym) is garbled.

issues.translation_quote: - Girl? - Chick.
issues.justification: The Russian gag is slang vs. English lesson; here the translation works, but 'Это Вася... младший научный сотрудник' follows with incoherent flow.

issues.source_quote: Вы ... английский язык... Выучить от сих до сих.
issues.translation_quote: you two... you, English... Learn it from here to here.
issues.justification: Awkward and unclear rendering; the original means 'you, English — learn it from this point to that point'.

issues.source_quote: Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал, сколько душ я загубил!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, how many I’ve stabbed, how many I’ve slashed, how many souls I’ve damned!
issues.justification: This is the parodic thieves' song ('Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал'); 'damned' misrenders 'загубил' (destroyed/ruined) and the rhythm of the parody is lost.

issues.translation_quote: We had a drink. Shut up!
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Устроили тут ромашка' rendered as 'he-loves-me, he-loves-me-not' loses the idiom 'устроили ромашку' (playing back-and-forth).

issues.source_quote: Если б мы еще шапка принесли! Доцент кто? Жулик.
issues.translation_quote: If only we bring the hat! Who is Docent? Crook.
issues.justification: The deliberately broken pidgin English for Vasya contradicts the original, where this sentence is spoken by Vasya in ordinary broken style only occasionally; inconsistency.

issues.translation_quote: What are you blowing smoke for?
issues.justification: 'Свистишь' here means 'lying/making things up'; the translation is somewhat unnatural.

issues.translation_quote: No, the cabbie swiped it. It was the cabbie for sure!
issues.justification: Fine; but the preceding 'Give tenner, I buy kerosene stove. - Primus very bad, fire can be.' pidgin dialect is applied inconsistently with Vasya's speech earlier.

issues.translation_quote: Sporting greetings!
issues.justification: The Soviet-era 'Физкульт-привет' catchphrase is only approximated; acceptable but loses period flavor.

issues.source_quote: Какая зараза хмыренку этому на Хмыря накапала?
issues.translation_quote: What lowlife snitched on Creep to that little creep?
issues.justification: Nickname 'Хмырь' inconsistently rendered as 'Creep', 'Little Creep' and 'Hmyr'; also confusing as the kid is 'хмыренок' (Hmyr's son).

issues.source_quote: Ты на третьем, ты на пятом!
issues.translation_quote: You take the third floor, you the fifth!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.translation_quote: It is an archaeological treasure of the most unique kind.
issues.justification: 'Most unique' is awkward; stiff phrasing in translation.

issues.source_quote: - Нет, не согласен. Почему? Смешно это.
issues.translation_quote: - No, I don't. Why? It's ridiculous.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Sort of. Well, tell me.
issues.justification: 'Вроде' as 'Sort of' is slightly off; 'Apparently' / 'So it seems' fits better.
